verdicts.note: Duplicate of the fertility-counselling practice chapter.
No abstract. Family policies and fertility in Europe — the comparison class for whether ART access matters relative to other levers.
Duplicate-shaped record of the ACA fertility-care commentary.
Sociology of the biomedical model of infertility.
No abstract. Economic and sociocultural factors in seeking fertility services.
GBD analysis of infertility at advanced maternal age. Wall 4, and it sizes the treatable population.
Pregnancy after 40 as a realized outcome.
Supply-chain framing of reproductive biotechnology.
Gendered infertility schemas, qualitative.
Reproductive surgery audit, Nigeria. Wall 8.
ART LEGAL COHERENCE across Europe with policy recommendations. Maps the legal-availability variation P2 needs, complementing the IFFS surveillance and age-limit records.
Oncofertility practice survey, Japan.
Preterm birth's contribution to infant mortality.
Family spillovers in health behaviour.
Billari et al. on the drivers of European postponement. A.15's core reference.
PAH metabolites and male infertility. B.2's.
AMH in late-reproductive-age fertility assessment.
GBD infertility epidemiology and forecasts.

**Norway 1967-2004: twinning rates decomposed into MATERNAL AGE and ART.** This is A.12's decomposition on Norwegian data — exactly the Pison/Monden/Smits exercise. Route with a flag; A.12's SDT arm turns on this split.
Quality of life 4-5.5 years after UNSUCCESSFUL IVF. Follows the failures, which most of the literature does not.
Liquidity sensitivity of healthcare consumption. The general form of arm 2's price channel.
Survey-mode methodology among cancer survivors.
Preterm birth trends in Flanders, attributed partly to multiple pregnancies.

UK population-level incidence of fertility problems presenting to PRIMARY CARE, with socioeconomic inequalities. The entry step under the NHS — a universal-access counterpart to the US utilisation records.
Oncofertility in developing countries.

**National survey of knowledge about age-related decline AND OOCYTE CRYOPRESERVATION together.** Sits on the P5/P6 seam: what women believe egg freezing can do is the belief most directly capable of inducing postponement.

Preservation coverage for transgender people — a medical indication distinct from both onco and elective. NOTE: Wall 5's binary indication split does not have a home for gender-affirming preservation; if such records recur, the taxonomy needs a third value.
Narrative review of medical students' fertility awareness. Fourth review of this cell.

US young adults' family-building intentions under hypothetical infertility AND their knowledge of COSTS. Belief about price as well as about biology — the two channels A.17 separates into arms, met inside one survey.
Relaxation interventions during ART.
Disposable diapers and later male fertility. B.6's.
Women's education and second-birth interval, China.
Frozen vs fresh transfer in low responders.
Meaning-of-parenthood scale, Portugal.
Cultural dynamics and economic theories of fertility. D.1's.
Bongaarts & Feeney on quantum and tempo. A.11's.
Lifestyle factors and reproductive performance.
Obesity and ART live-birth rates per cycle. Wall 1 by outcome — but it is the evidence base for the BMI eligibility rationing seen in P2.

**'THE SPONTANEOUS PREGNANCY PROGNOSIS IN UNTREATED SUBFERTILE COUPLES' — the Walcheren primary care study.** The counterfactual measured on the untreated, in primary care rather than in a clinic sample. This is the single cleanest statement of what arm 1 sets to zero, and it is the record the chapter's upper-bound section should be built around. Highest priority.

**The International Fertility Decision-making Study — fertility knowledge and BELIEFS ABOUT TREATMENT across many countries.** The largest and most comparable measurement of P6's belief side; beliefs about treatment specifically, not age knowledge in general.
No abstract. DECLINING estimates of US infertility 1982-2002. Wall 4, but a striking fact for the chapter's framing: the treatable population may not be growing.
Psychosocial experience of fertility problems.
CDC ART Surveillance 2001 — the earliest US edition in the frame, typed `dataset`.
No abstract. 'Why Do Women Wait?' — matching and wage inequality as causes of delay. A.15/C.7's, and the economic complement to the JET option-value paper.
Prevalence of subfertility, review.
Which infertility definition to use.
Air quality and ART outcomes.
Ovarian tissue cryopreservation and transplantation, scientific review. **Indication NOT NAMED — a Wall 5 residue case, and exactly the kind the 17% figure refers to.**
ESHRE register data for Europe with a detailed DENMARK description — Denmark is the register population arm 1's best work uses.
Danish first-pregnancy-planner cohort design.
Coping after unsuccessful treatment.
Diagnostic pathway for the infertile couple.
'Can policies enhance fertility in Europe?' — the Gauthier/Philipov debate. The benchmark the demographic-significance stage needs: how large any policy effect on fertility has ever been.

**DECLINING REALISATION OF REPRODUCTIVE INTENTIONS WITH AGE — likelihood of a birth within 4 years, for men and women.** Intentions measured against realized births at successive ages. The behaviour side of P6 with a real outcome and a panel horizon.
Characteristics of advanced-age first-time mothers.
Marital fertility specification by age at marriage. A.7's.
No abstract. Still-childless Swedes aged 28-40 and their reproductive intentions.
Economic implications of ART multiple pregnancy.

**FOLLOW-UP OF COUPLES WHO DROPPED OUT of a specialist fertility clinic.** Sixth counterfactual record. Between the Walcheren untreated-prognosis study, the Japanese dropout study, the 8-year seven-in-ten study and this one, arm 1's zero-counterfactual assumption is now contradicted by a coherent set rather than by one paper.
Companion piece in the pronatalist-policy debate: what fertility indicators can and cannot tell policymakers. Bears on PI call 4.
